Subject: Dedicated APAC pool (Singapore) — initial sizing/context

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week — we took the internal product sync and kicked off a capacity plan. ClearData AI is aiming to move our inference traffic for core search and document-qa to a dedicated APAC pool (Singapore) to meet latency and data residency needs for several enterprise customers in the region.

High-level numbers from our side (early estimates):
- Steady-state: ~200 qps peak (requests/sec) across light and heavy prompts; burst to 600 qps for product launches.
- Per-request token profile: avg input 120 tokens, expected output 220 tokens. Estimate ~1.4B tokens/month initially.
- Models: two variants (open LLM v1.3, and a finetuned smaller reranker). We need the ability to route heavier generation to larger instances and keep reranking cheap.
- Latency target: 95th <= 450ms for short prompts; 99th < 900ms where possible.
- Timeline: want pool live by end of Sep 2026 for staggered onboarding.

Can you share a sizing recommendation and rough pricing guidance? We also have procurement/legal notes we can send after an initial estimate.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m call if needed.

Kevin Li
Head of Infrastructure
ClearData AI

Summary / proposal (high level) — focused on APAC greenfield sizing with options:

Option A (conservative, lower cost ramp)
- Persistent pool: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent inference nodes (persistent) optimized for throughput and caching.
- Burst capacity: 3 x burst nodes available for launches (elastic; charged on use).
- Expected steady concurrency: ~40 concurrent streams at 512-token avg; supports ~200 qps steady with prefix caching.
- Estimated monthly tokens handled: ~1.0–1.6B depending on cache hit rate and batching.
- Latency: 95th ~350–500ms for short prompts; 99th under 900ms in normal conditions.

Option B (latency/SLA-first)
- Persistent: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes + 2 burst nodes.
- Persistent concurrency: ~60 concurrent streams; handles bursts more gracefully without cold starts.
- Estimated tokens/month: 1.4–2.2B.

Operational notes / risk tradeoffs
- Quantization: recommend mixed-precision for the main generator; keep reranker in FP16 for stability. This reduces cost while preserving tail quality.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for high-reuse inference paths (search QA), which materially reduces token run-rate.
- Rollout: start with a canary routing 10% -> APAC pool for two weeks, progressively increase while monitoring latency and cost.
- Fallbacks: route to EU pool in cross-region fallback if APAC capacity exhausted (short-term) — needs routing policy approval and data residency check.

Next steps / asks for proposal finalization
- Confirm target SLO split (percent <=450ms).
- Confirm expected sustained burst duration.
- Any hard requirements around KMS/HSM or VPC peering for private connectivity?

Attaching a short proposal PDF (apac-pool-proposal-v1.pdf) and an exec note for Marissa's pricing reference.

Marcus Lin
Capacity Planning Lead | Redwood Inference

Kevin / Jane — thanks for the quick turn. Attached is our recommended proposal (APAC Option B) and an executive commitment note with the commercial starting point. Key points below:

Proposal highlights (recommended: Option B)
- Persistent pool: 6 inference nodes (A100-80GB equiv) + 2 burst nodes
- Support for two model classes with routing policy and quantization profile per model
- Canary plan: 10% -> APAC for 2 weeks, then 30% -> 60% increments across 4 weeks
- Onboarding timeline: contract + SOC2 evidence clearance + network setup = target go-live by 2026-09-28

Commercial ballpark
- Monthly platform fee (reserved persistent pool): $62,000/month (covers persistent nodes + observability/trace retention)
- Burst usage billed at $X per node-hour (estimated additional $6–12k/month depending on launch cadence)
- One-time onboarding: $12,500 (network, delivery runbooks, runbook drills)

Action items we need from ClearData AI
1) Confirm SLO split: percent of traffic that must meet <=450ms (we used 70% in our sizing).
2) Confirm whether VPC peering + customer KMS is required.
3) Sign the MSA and initial 3-month commitment (we propose 60% of persistent capacity reserved for Q4 as a Show-of-Commitment).
